article_content: Hollywood studios are prioritizing sequels and reboots following significant 2012 box office failures. Industry reports confirm 31 sequels and 17 reboots scheduled for 2013, including new installments of X-Men, Fast & Furious, Die Hard, and Iron Man franchises. This strategy follows major financial losses from original films like Disney's John Carter, resulting in a $123 million write-off and executive resignations. Other underperformers include Universal's Battleship ($209M budget) and The Oogieloves, which recouped only $1 million of its $20 million budget. Industry analyst Keith Simanton observed: 'Audiences prefer familiar franchises, making original projects financially riskier.' Successful franchise films like Avengers ($1.5B global gross) and The Hangover Part II ($580M) continue shaping studio strategies despite mixed critical reception.

article_content: Labour has raised concerns that reduced police funding is resulting in fewer rape convictions. Official data reveals a troubling trend: reported rape cases increased by 30% between 2011-2014, while arrests decreased by 8%. Analysis of 32 UK police forces (of 43 total) shows 16,983 reported cases last year - up nearly 4,000 - but arrests fell by approximately 1,000 to 10,710. Conviction rates dropped from one in seven (14%) to one in ten (10%), with prosecutions declining from one in four (25%) to under one in five (20%) of reported cases. Labour MP Seema Malhotra stated: 'These figures expose the devastating justice gap created by current policies. More survivors face barriers to justice while fewer perpetrators face consequences.' Malhotra attributed this to cuts in specialist police units and warned of planned future reductions, pledging Labour would reverse these measures if elected.

article_content: By Claudia Connell | Published: 29 May 2013 The mundane task of loading dishwashers gains novelty through homemade vodka infusions. The 'dishwasher vodka' trend involves combining sweets or chocolate with vodka, using a dishwasher's heat (70°C cycle) to blend flavors while preserving alcohol content. We tested 10 variations: Method: Fill 1-liter bottles with 200g (hard/boiled sweets) or 300g (chocolate/jelly sweets). Remove one-third vodka, add ingredients, seal with cling film. Run empty dishwasher without detergent. Shake before and after cycle. Strain if needed. Serve chilled within 7 days. Results: 1. Pear Drops: Powdered version created smooth orange liquid with strong flavor (150g sufficient). 2. Jelly Babies: Chopping required. Red variants yielded weak taste despite pink hue. 3. After Eights: Multiple strains needed for mint-chocolate blend. Rich flavor, unappealing texture. 4. Liquorice: Overpowering taste with murky appearance. 5. Skittles: Mixed flavors produced zesty drink with temporary surface residue. 6. Gummy Bears: Effortless infusion, ideal shot drink with citrus color. 7. Werther's Originals: Optimal dissolution for caramel vodka resembling bar cocktails. Conclusion: Hard sweets performed best. Store frozen; consume within a week.

While companies haven't disclosed specific reasons, analysts cite likely factors including projected consumer reluctance to absorb additional hardware costs or subscription fees. This development underscores how market forces influence technological priorities. Existing satellite communication options like Apple's emergency feature remain available, with ongoing development from Google, T-Mobile/Starlink, and Motorola. Industry trends show manufacturers continue focusing on mainstream upgrades like camera improvements rather than niche innovations without clear revenue potential. This pattern echoes past tech cycles where early-adopter products faced market challenges.

article_content: Archaeologists have solved a 200-year mystery surrounding the 170kg 'Bosham Head,' a massive stone artifact found in a Chichester garden. Using advanced 3D scanning technology, researchers from Bournemouth University determined the weathered sculpture—twice the size of a human head—dates back to 122 AD and depicts Emperor Trajan. The team, led by Dr. Miles Russell and Harry Manley, collaborated with The Novium museum for their analysis. Historical records indicate Trajan ruled Rome from 98 AD until his death, overseeing significant military campaigns and public works. The statue, carved from Italian marble, was likely erected by Trajan's successor Hadrian during his 121-122 AD British travels. Standing at Chichester Harbour's entrance, it would have welcomed visitors as a symbol of Roman authority. Despite centuries of erosion and possible submersion in seawater—which contributed to its weathered appearance—laser scans revealed distinct facial features and hairstyle patterns matching Trajan's known depictions. Dr. Russell emphasized the artifact's importance: 'This isn't just local history—it's a monumental greeting from the Roman Empire to all of Southern England.' A comparable Trajan statue exists at Rome's Ostia Harbour, highlighting imperial connections between Britain and the Mediterranean. The rediscovered head now resides at Fishbourne's Collection Discovery Centre, finally receiving recognition after years of being overlooked.

article_content: Israeli military operations have intensified Gaza's humanitarian crisis, compounding 16 years of blockade. Over 5,000 Palestinians, mostly civilians, have been killed in two weeks of bombardment according to UN estimates. Survivors face severe shortages of essentials including clean water and medicine. Even before current hostilities, over 60% of Gaza's 2.3 million residents relied on food aid. The UN describes the situation as 'catastrophic' following Israel's suspension of critical supplies. Gaza's food systems have collapsed under bombardment, with agencies now providing just one daily bread ration. Limited aid convoys have entered via Egypt, with numerous trucks reportedly awaiting approval. Bombed bakeries and power shortages constrain food production. Kifah Qudeh, sheltering at a UN facility, describes rationing four water bottles and three bread pieces every three days for his family: 'We split bread with whatever we can find - sometimes just plain. It's barely enough.' Nutritionist Yusra Eshaq explains reduced caloric intake forces bodies to consume muscle mass, risking organ failure. Psychotherapist Iman Farajallah contrasts pre-blockade meals of fresh produce with current processed food dependence. Gaza's aquifer is 97% contaminated per WHO standards. Damaged infrastructure and fuel shortages disrupt water access. Qudeh notes his family's strict rationing: 'We drink one glass daily - must make it last.' Medical experts warn dehydration causes rapid health deterioration, particularly in children.

article_content: Media mogul Rupert Murdoch, chairman of News Corporation, critiqued Australia's renewable energy investments during a Sky News interview with The Australian's Paul Kelly. He characterized wind energy projects as financially burdensome with questionable efficacy, stating coastal adaptation should precede emission reduction efforts. 'When seas rise, nations like the Maldives face existential threats - realities we must pragmatically address,' Murdoch asserted. While recognizing long-term climate patterns, Murdoch downplayed Australia's carbon footprint relative to global emitters. He advocated prioritizing affordable energy markets over environmental measures, simultaneously praising former Prime Minister Tony Abbott as 'an admirable leader worthy of public trust.' The media magnate cautioned against premature assessments of current policies, noting 'governing complexities require time for proper evaluation.' On international relations, Murdoch urged strengthened Asian economic ties, particularly with China: 'Cooperation beats confrontation. Our shared interests outweigh environmental disagreements.' He dismissed notions of Chinese expansionism, advocating practical diplomacy focused on mutual benefit.

article_content: By Sarah Griffiths | Published: 07:03 EST, 27 June 2013 | Updated: 07:03 EST, 27 June 2013 New research indicates trolls are motivated by power, amusement, boredom, and revenge, exploiting online anonymity. Dr. Claire Hardaker from Lancaster University studied 4,000 trolling cases, revealing systematic provocation tactics. The phenomenon disrupts digital spaces through insults and threats, sometimes escalating to cyberstalking. While framed as free speech by some, Dr. Hardaker's research in the Journal of Language, Aggression and Conflict identifies seven key strategies: 1. Shifting discussions to sensitive topics 2. Hypocritically criticizing others' writing errors 3. Using faux-naive questions to create moral dilemmas 4. Providing harmful advice disguised as help 5. Deliberate taboo violations to shock audiences 6. Direct personal attacks without justification 7. Spamming multiple groups with off-topic content The study shows trolling's evolution beyond obvious abuse to sophisticated disruption techniques. With rising cyberbullying-related suicides, Dr. Hardaker stresses that trolls span all age groups. Both celebrities like Jessie J and ordinary users face targeted attacks.

article_content: U.S. Army psychiatrist Major Nidal Hasan, convicted of the November 2009 Fort Hood shooting that killed 13 people and injured 30, has been forcibly shaved per military regulations. Army spokesman Lt. Col. S. Justin Platt confirmed the action Tuesday. Hasan maintained a beard post-attack, citing religious reasons, which delayed his court-martial for over three months due to grooming standard conflicts. Following his August 2013 death sentence at Fort Hood proceedings, Hasan was transferred to Fort Leavenworth's military death row. While trial judge Col. article_content: The U.S. Navy successfully intercepted a non-functional spy satellite on February 20, 2008, preventing potential toxic gas contamination. Using a modified Standard Missile-3 launched from the USS Lake Erie in the Pacific, the operation targeted the satellite's hydrazine fuel tank approximately 247 km (133 nautical miles) above Earth. Defense officials confirmed the intercept through multi-sensor networks but required 24 hours to verify fuel tank destruction. The satellite, launched in 2006, contained 1,000 pounds of frozen hydrazine - a toxic compound posing respiratory risks. Without intervention, it would have re-entered Earth's atmosphere in early March 2008, potentially releasing hazardous fumes over a two-football-field area. The $60 million operation followed space shuttle Atlantis' safe return to avoid debris collisions. While U.S. officials framed this as a public safety measure, China expressed concerns about space militarization, referencing their 2007 satellite destruction that created over 100,000 orbital debris fragments. Military planners timed the intercept to minimize space debris risks, with most fragments expected to burn up within 48 hours.

article_content: An intriguing enigma reminiscent of spy novels has emerged from the South Pacific. Scientists from Australia recently investigated a landmass called Sandy Island, visible on Google Earth and various nautical charts midway between Australia and New Caledonia. Their expedition revealed only open ocean where maps indicated terrain. The phantom island first appeared in digital records around 2000 through National Geographic's mapping systems. While some sources like the 1999 Times Atlas showed empty waters, discrepancies persisted across platforms. Maritime researchers aboard the Southern Surveyor vessel recorded sea depths exceeding 1,400 meters (4,620 feet) at the coordinates, confirming no shallow seabed that could support an island. Cartography experts suggest possible explanations ranging from historical data errors to deliberate 'trap' placements in maps. French hydrographic records indicate the anomaly should have been removed in 1979. Google Maps representatives acknowledged the challenge of maintaining current global data, using multiple sources that sometimes conflict. Social media reactions ranged from technical discussions about satellite imaging limitations to various conspiracy theories. While most urban areas receive frequent aerial photography updates, remote regions like the Coral Sea often rely on older satellite data with lower resolution.

article_content: Afghan President Hamid Karzai declared Monday that military operations to liberate Kandahar from Taliban control will only commence with explicit public approval. White House spokesperson Robert Gibbs expressed mounting frustrations while reaffirming respect for Karzai's democratic mandate. Current military deployments total approximately 100,000 American personnel alongside 40,000 NATO troops. While coalition forces successfully regained control of Marjah in early 2024, the Kandahar campaign faces postponements as local leaders voice safety apprehensions. General Stanley McChrystal, attending Sunday's tribal council, expressed continued confidence in operational collaborations despite political disagreements. Karzai reinforced Afghanistan's autonomous status, asserting: 'International partners provide support, but Afghans maintain leadership.' His upcoming May visit to Washington remains scheduled, though diplomatic ties appear strained amid ongoing disputes about military coordination timelines.

article_content: (CNN) -- Sid Caesar, the legendary comedian and star of NBC's groundbreaking 'Your Show of Shows' (1950-1954) who passed away in 2014, left behind a rich legacy of wit and wisdom. Known for revolutionizing television comedy, Caesar frequently emphasized truth as comedy's foundation: 'Comedy has to be based on truth. You take the truth and you put a little curlicue at the end.' His signature blend of self-deprecating humor and sharp observation shone through remarks like: 'When I did comedy I made fun of myself. If there was a buffoon, I played the buffoon.' Caesar's philosophical side emerged in musings such as: 'There's a now, a was, and a gonna be... It hasn't happened yet. It's gonna happen as soon as the now is over.' His innovative approach continues to influence comedians worldwide.

article_content: Two Florida men who survived death row convictions are now advocating against a controversial capital punishment bill. Seth Penalver and Herman Lindsey, both cleared of murder charges after years of imprisonment, urged Governor Rick Scott to reject legislation that would accelerate execution timelines. The proposed 'Timely Justice Act' mandates death warrants within 30 days of state Supreme Court reviews and executions within 180 days thereafter. Supporters argue it streamlines justice, while critics warn it risks executing innocent people by limiting appeal options. 'This law would've killed me before proving my innocence,' stated Penalver, released in 2022 after new evidence emerged post-appeals. Lindsey, exonerated following three years on death row, added: 'It guarantees wrongful executions.' The bill's sponsor, Representative Matt Gaetz, countered that modern legal safeguards prevent such outcomes. Florida leads nationally in death row exonerations, with 24 cases overturned. ACLU director Howard Simon noted the state's 13-year average death row tenure aligns closely with the 14-year national pattern, disputing claims of excessive delays. The legislation faces final approval decision by mid-June.

This incident follows increased Houthi attacks on regional shipping, including ballistic missiles fired toward US ships from Houthi-controlled territory after the hijacking attempt. Yemen's Aden-based government blamed the Houthis for the attack, though the group claimed no responsibility. article_content: USDA reports indicate over 8.3 million American children experience food insecurity, facing uncertainty about their next meal. This reality deeply impacted Justin and Kate Rose after relocating from England to Orlando ten years ago. While familiar with poverty in South Africa through family connections, they were stunned by America's childhood hunger crisis - stemming not from scarcity but systemic distribution issues and nutritional disparities. As parents (Justin being a PGA Tour champion) raising their son Leo, the Roses noticed direct correlations between diet and children's behavior. This raised concerns about undernourished students' academic capabilities. Though school meal programs provide weekday support, many families struggle through weekends. Partnering with Blessings in a Backpack, a nonprofit supplying weekend meals at $100 annually per child, the Roses initiated local aid. Their Orlando program now assists 1,600 weekly. Heartrending stories of families stretching backpack provisions or resorting to toothpaste for sustenance inspired them to found the Kate and Justin Rose Foundation. The foundation's comprehensive approach features school gardens for fresh produce, educational book stipends, and cultural field trips. Juggling family responsibilities with philanthropy, the Roses champion gradual impact: 'Nourishing and educating one child at a time creates lasting change.'

article_content: Lululemon founder Chip Wilson has issued a public apology following controversial remarks about women's bodies being incompatible with the company's yoga pants. The November 13, 2013 apology video addresses backlash from Wilson's earlier Bloomberg interview statement that 'some women's bodies just don't actually work' for the product line. This follows a March 2013 recall of 17% of Lululemon's yoga pants due to manufacturing-related sheerness issues. The company reported a $20 million financial impact, with CEO Christine Day announcing her June resignation. Wilson's comments intensified criticism, with many questioning the apology's sincerity. The company introduced Full-On Luon pants ($72-$98) featuring redesigned fabric undergoing 13-15 quality tests per batch. Despite claims of improved opacity, customer reviews note persistent pilling and transparency issues, contrasting with promotional materials showing successful stress-testing.

Hakan ya biyo bayan kamfanin ya mayar da kashi 17% na wandunan yoga a watan Maris 2013 saboda matsalolin gani ta hanyar masana'anta. Kamfanin ya sami asarar dala miliyan 20, kuma Shugaba Christine Day ta sanar da murabus dinta a watan Yuni. Kalaman Wilson sun kara tsananta sukar, da yawa suna tambayar gaskiyar hakuri. Kamfanin ya gabatar da sabbin wandunan Full-On Luon ($72-$98) waɗanda ke da sabon zane na yadi da aka duba ta hanyar gwaje-gwaje 13-15 a kowane rukuni. Duk da ikirarin ingantaccen gani, sharhin abokan ciniki sun lura da ci gaba da matsalolin zubar da fure da gani, suna sabanin kayan talla da ke nuna nasarar gwajin matsi.

article_content: (CNN) -- After an intensive ground and air search across northern Colorado, authorities found 6-year-old Falcon Heene concealed in his family's attic. The child admitted hiding in a storage box during the entire operation, stating: 'I played with my toys and took a nap.' His father, meteorologist Richard Heene, expressed regret to reporters: 'I apologize for shouting at him. He says that's why he hid.' The emergency response began following reports of a drifting experimental helium balloon (6 meters long, 1.5 meters high) that initially appeared to carry the child. The silver craft reached 2,100 meters altitude before landing 145 kilometers away. Colorado Air National Guard helicopters were deployed as a precaution before Falcon's safe discovery. Larimer County Sheriff James Alderden explained: 'Children often hide during large searches fearing punishment.' The family's background as storm researchers and their 2009 reality TV appearance attracted media scrutiny. Neighbors confirmed the balloon was designed for atmospheric research, not human transport, describing the Heenes as 'eccentric but well-meaning science enthusiasts.'

article_content: Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar formally apologized in the state assembly on November 9 following widespread criticism of his remarks about women's education and population control. During Tuesday's winter session, Kumar had linked increased female education to reduced fertility rates, noting Bihar's decline from 4.3% to 2.9% based on recent data. His choice of language sparked immediate backlash, with BJP leaders accusing him of using vulgar terminology and women legislators condemning perceived disrespect. Deputy CM Tejashwi Yadav clarified that Kumar's comments addressed the role of school-based sex education in population management. 'These discussions are part of scientific curriculum, not inappropriate remarks,' Yadav stated. However, BJP MLA Nikki Hembrom maintained that Kumar's phrasing demonstrated insensitivity toward women, calling for more dignified discourse from leadership.

A zaman majalisar hunturu ranar Talata, Kumar ya bayyana cewa ilimin mata yana taimakawa rage adadin haihuwa, yana nuni da raguwar adadin haihuwa daga kashi 4.3% zuwa 2.9% a cikin 'yan shekarun nan. 'Wannan ba batanci ba ne, a'a yana cikin ilimin kimiyya da halittu,' in ji Yadav. Duk da haka, 'yar majalisar BJP Nikki Hembrom ta nuna rashin amincewa, tana mai cewa kalaman sun nuna rashin mutuntawa ga mata.

article_content: A passenger involved in a United Airlines seat reclining dispute has expressed partial regret while defending his use of the Knee Defender device. James Beach, a Colorado businessman, acknowledged poor conflict resolution during an August 24 flight from Newark to Denver but maintained ambiguity about future device usage. The altercation occurred when Beach used the $22 gadget to block seat reclining in United's Economy Plus section, which offers 5 extra inches of legroom compared to standard seats. After complying with a flight attendant's request to remove the device, Beach claims the front passenger abruptly reclined, nearly damaging his laptop. A subsequent physical altercation involving seat pushing and drink-throwing forced an unscheduled landing in Chicago. While neither passenger faced arrest, aviation commentator Johnny 'Jet' DiScala criticized the $6,000/hour diversion cost. Knee Defender inventor Ira Goldman highlighted systemic issues: 'Airlines sell the same physical space twice - legroom and recline space.' Major carriers including Delta, American, and Southwest (which operates AirTran) prohibit the device despite no FAA ban. Goldman argues the device protects passengers from injury and equipment damage, accusing airlines of ignoring ergonomic conflicts.

article_content: Albert Einstein revolutionized physics through Gedankenexperiments (German for 'thought experiments') that blended theory with empirical data. These mental exercises produced his seminal theories of special (1905) and general (1915) relativity. At 16, Einstein contemplated light's nature: Traveling at light speed would seemingly freeze its electromagnetic waves - an impossibility that hinted at special relativity. Train-based scenarios later showed observers disagreeing about simultaneous events due to relative motion's effects on light perception. The twin paradox demonstrates time dilation: A spacefaring twin ages slower than their Earth-bound counterpart. Tools like Omni Calculator quantify this effect - at near-light speeds, decades could pass on Earth while only years elapse for travelers. Einstein's elevator analogy proved gravity's equivalence to acceleration. Without visual cues, occupants can't distinguish between gravitational pull and upward thrust. This principle revealed gravity as spacetime curvature, visualized by massive objects bending a trampoline-like fabric - central to general relativity. Despite relativity breakthroughs, Einstein rejected quantum theory's 'spooky action.' His entanglement critique used split metaphorical coins representing particle pairs. Contrary to his hidden variables theory, 2022 Nobel physicists confirmed entanglement's instantaneous correlations across vast distances.

Sabanin ka'idar sa na ɓoyayyun masu canji, masana kimiyyar Nobel na 2022 sun tabbatar da haɗin gwiwar ta'aziyya tsakanin nisa mai yawa.

article_content: A major wildfire near Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico has triggered evacuations for more than 10,000 residents as firefighters combat extreme weather conditions. Officials reported Monday that approximately 8,000 additional residents were advised to evacuate, following 3,000 who left under voluntary orders Sunday night. The Las Conchas fire, which ignited over the weekend, had reached within one mile of the laboratory's southwestern boundary by Monday afternoon. Burning across nearly 44,000 acres with 0% containment, the blaze has also caused a smaller one-acre fire on the lab's southern perimeter. Laboratory spokesman Kevin Roark stated: 'While we're monitoring closely, our critical facilities remain secure. We're prepared to manage this threat effectively.' The nuclear research center, employing over 11,000 staff, suspended nonessential operations through Tuesday. Senator Jeff Bingaman reassured the public: 'The lab implemented robust fire safety protocols. Essential structures are well-protected.' The Department of Energy facility, located 35 miles northwest of Santa Fe, partners with major contractors including Bechtel National, the University of California, Babcock & Wilcox, and URS Washington Division.

Jami'ai sun ruwaito cewa kimanin mazauna 8,000 an ba su umarnin fice daga gidajensu a ranar Litinin, bayan 3,000 da suka bar gida bisa son rai a ranar Lahadi. article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) -- Charging women with larger busts more for bras doesn't win public support, British retailer Marks & Spencer acknowledged Friday as it ended surcharges on larger lingerie sizes. The company apologized for its pricing policy. 'We boobed,' stated a full-page Marks & Spencer advertisement in British newspapers. The retailer responded to campaigners arguing that higher prices for larger bras were unfair. Previously, Marks & Spencer charged up to £2 ($3) more for sizes DD and above. 'While our quality larger bras cost more to produce, we recognize it was wrong to pass this cost to customers,' the ad stated. This follows a year-long campaign by Facebook group Busts 4 Justice. Campaigners noted other retailers don't charge extra for larger sizes, arguing Marks & Spencer should follow suit. They highlighted the store's standard clothing pricing doesn't vary by size. Group administrators Becky Mount and Beckie Williams posted: 'We thank supporters, especially thousands of women who joined our cause. Busts 4 Justice remains committed to improving options for fuller-busted women, but we're pleased to now encourage all women to purchase fairly priced, well-fitting lingerie.' Marks & Spencer, known for affordable basics, also announced a 25% discount on all bras through May. Mount added: 'While some resented buying M&S bras due to surcharges, we should appreciate their policy change and generous discount. Stores might sell out quickly!'

Kamfanin ya nemi gafarar jama'a game da manufar farashinsa. 'Mun yi kuskure,' in ji wani cikakken shafi na tallan Marks & Spencer a cikin jaridun Biritaniya. article_content: London – British Muslim cleric Anjem Choudary has proposed a controversial march through Wootton Bassett, the town where fallen British soldiers are traditionally repatriated, sparking widespread criticism. Choudary's organization Islam4UK claims the demonstration would highlight opposition to the Afghanistan conflict, alleging Western forces commit 'murderous crimes' to serve political agendas. Authorities confirm no formal protest application has been submitted. Over 215,000 people joined a Facebook group opposing the planned march within 24 hours of its announcement. Prime Minister Gordon Brown condemned Choudary's views as 'a perverted interpretation of Islam,' emphasizing mainstream Muslim communities reject such extremism. Wiltshire Police stated they retain authority to impose restrictions or prohibit the march if public safety concerns emerge. Choudary's open letter referenced support for Osama Bin Laden and characterized Afghanistan as 'Muslim land' undeserving of foreign occupation.

article_content: A four-year-old boy has died after being struck by a falling mirror at the Hugo Boss store in Bicester Village, Oxfordshire. The incident occurred on Tuesday evening at approximately 8:40 PM while the child was shopping with his family. Emergency services transported him to John Radcliffe Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries after four days of treatment. Thames Valley Police have launched an investigation and are urging witnesses present in the store during the incident to come forward. Detective Inspector Steve Duffy stated: 'Our thoughts are with the family. We're investigating the circumstances and request anyone with information to contact us urgently.' Both Hugo Boss and Bicester Village released statements expressing deep sadness and offering condolences. The store remains closed indefinitely, with the company cooperating fully with authorities. Oxfordshire County Council's Environmental Health department is assisting the police investigation, while the Health and Safety Executive confirmed local authorities lead retail safety oversight.

Muna ci gaba da bincike kuma muna buƙatar duk wanda ke da wani labari ya tuntube mu cikin sauri.' article_content: A Cardiff restaurant sparked controversy by sharing CCTV footage of four diners who allegedly left without paying their £80 bill. Burger & Lobster's new The Hayes location posted images suggesting the group might have forgotten to settle their meal tab, later confirming the family returned to pay in full. The restaurant donated the amount to Safer Wales charity following resolution. While management stated intentions focused on recovering payment rather than public shaming, the social media post drew mixed reactions. Critics condemned the identification method as unethical, with some patrons threatening boycotts. Supporters argued businesses must protect revenue, noting most customers pay without incident. The incident occurred at a chain known for its £20-per-item menu (burger, lobster, or lobster roll), marking Cardiff as its first UK location outside London. Company representatives acknowledged reviewing social media policies after removing the controversial post.

article_content: Early screenings of Darren Aronofsky's upcoming biblical epic 'Noah' have generated controversy due to differing interpretations between the director and studio executives. The $125 million film, co-produced by Paramount Pictures and New Regency Productions, underwent test screenings with faith-based audiences in New York (predominantly Jewish), Arizona (primarily Christian), and California (mixed demographics), receiving mixed responses. Aronofsky, known for Academy Award-nominated films 'Black Swan' and 'The Wrestler,' has described Noah as 'the first environmentalist' and revealed his lifelong connection to the story, having first written a prize-winning poem about the biblical figure in seventh grade. While some attendees praised the initial trailer shown at the Echo Conference (organized by a Texas-based church group), critics argue the film diverges significantly from biblical sources. Industry observers note tensions between the director's vision and studio expectations, with marketing consultant Mark Joseph warning about alienating core audiences. The production notably uses computer-generated animals rather than live creatures, a creative decision by Aronofsky.

article_content: A Catholic news outlet has published a graphic video purportedly showing Syrian rebels beheading a monk. Catholic Online released the footage on Monday, claiming it documents the June 23 execution of three individuals in Syria's Idlib province, including Father Francois Murad. The website warns viewers: 'DO NOT access this link unless you're above 18 and prepared for such material.' The report alleges the attackers invoked religious justification, speaking Arabic with what's described as a 'broken accent.' Bystanders appeared to record the executions with mobile devices. Catholic Online emphasized: 'Christians worldwide must understand the jihadist threat. Martyrdom remains a present danger, not just historical.' Vatican officials confirmed Murad's death last week but stated they hadn't verified the video's authenticity. The Custodians of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem similarly reported no knowledge of such footage. Catholic Online cited local sources attributing the attack to Jabhat al-Nusra, a U.S.-designated terrorist group. The incident highlights growing concerns about Christian communities in conflict zones. Syria's civil war has displaced millions, with religious minorities caught between Alawite Muslim-led government forces and Sunni Muslim-dominated rebel groups. Recent years have seen increased violence against Christians in Iraq, Egypt, and Syria. The Vatican's statement detailed Murad's death in Gassanieh village, noting his attempt to protect nuns before being killed. Over 100,000 fatalities have been recorded since Syria's conflict began in 2011, with all sides accused of atrocities.

article_content: (CNN) -- Individuals arrested in California should be aware that police can now legally search their cell phones' contents without a warrant. On Monday, the California Supreme Court ruled that law enforcement may examine data on arrested persons' mobile devices under existing search incident-to-arrest exceptions. The decision cites U.S. Supreme Court precedents regarding personal property searches during arrests. Justices Kathryn Mickle Werdegar and Carlos Moreno dissented, arguing smartphones' extensive data storage capacity requires stronger Fourth Amendment protections. The ruling stems from a 2007 Ventura County case where police found text messages referencing '6 pills of Ecstasy for $80' in Gregory Diaz's phone following a drug arrest. Authorities may access various data types including messages, photos, browsing history, and location information. While police cannot compel passcode disclosure without judicial approval, ACLU attorney Catherine Crump notes data copying legality remains unresolved. Civil liberties advocates warn this could impact protest-related arrests. Conflicting rulings with Ohio courts may prompt U.S. Supreme Court review.

article_content: Brian McClellen, a 21-year-old aspiring actor and model, tragically passed away Monday after sustaining severe injuries during a train-surfing incident. The Ohio native was discovered burning on a Metro-North train roof in Greenwich early Sunday morning, suffering burns covering 85% of his body. MTA spokesperson Aaron Donovan confirmed McClellen likely contacted a pantograph - the train's power-collecting apparatus - causing immediate ignition. Crew members extinguished the flames, but the injuries proved fatal. McClellen, a Cleveland native and North Royalton HS alumnus, had recently secured acting roles in TV's 'Younger' and film project 'Urge.' His agent Ryan Colby confirmed he'd chosen the Hilary Duff series shortly before the accident. Social media overflowed with tributes, including heartfelt messages from family and friends remembering his vibrant personality and daring spirit. Authorities continue investigating how McClellen accessed the train's roof as passengers were safely transferred following the incident.

article_content: American comedian Bill Burr sparked controversy upon arriving in Perth for his Australian tour commencement on Australia Day. During a podcast recorded prior to his visit, the Breaking Bad actor suggested Australia should emulate America's approach of granting casinos to Indigenous communities rather than pursuing land restitution. Burr drew parallels between colonial histories while explaining Australia Day to US listeners, referencing Midnight Oil's protest anthem 'Beds Are Burning.' He quipped that instead of returning land as the song advocates, authorities should 'just give them casinos like we did and move on.' Tasmanian Aboriginal Centre's Michael Mansell condemned the remarks as 'racist,' arguing they perpetuate stereotypes about Indigenous economic capabilities. The comedian acknowledged his limited grasp of Australian history during the broadcast, comparing it to America's colonial past. Burr sarcastically recited lyrics from the 1987 track while questioning the practicality of land return, noting former singer Peter Garrett's subsequent political career as Labor minister under PMs Rudd and Gillard. While Burr emphasized his commentary shouldn't be taken seriously, Mansell maintained such humor minimizes historical trauma. The Indigenous advocate highlighted contradictions in celebrating colonial history while dismissing Indigenous perspectives: 'If atrocities from 200 years ago still affect communities today, why should we forget?'

After a pursuit into the subway station, multiple witnesses including fellow officers testified they saw Kern assault Mineo with a baton. Brooklyn DA Charles Hynes praised the cooperating officers' actions as 'responsible, if not heroic.' Medical evidence from hospital staff and police labs corroborated Mineo's account. Defense attorneys claim the case lacks substance and suggest Mineo seeks financial gain through a planned lawsuit, while prosecutors maintain forensic proof supports the charges. Mineo states he continues experiencing trauma from the attack.

article_content: Telangana Minister and BRS leader KTR Rao criticized Congress leader Rahul Gandhi during his visit to Nizamabad district ahead of state elections. Rao labeled Gandhi as 'Pappu', claiming he lacks knowledge of Telangana's history. He demanded Gandhi apologize for the Congress-led merger of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh from 1956 until Telangana's formation in 2014. Rao stated: 'Rahul Gandhi's great-grandfather Jawaharlal Nehru, as Prime Minister, oversaw the 1956 merger. Before seeking votes, he must apologize for this historical decision.' Telangana was officially created in 2014 after decades of political movements, with K Chandrasekhar Rao becoming its first Chief Minister on June 2, 2014. In response, Rahul Gandhi accused BRS leader KCR and his family of controlling key revenue-generating ministries related to land, liquor, and sand. He alleged corruption in the Dalit Bandhu scheme and diversion of SC/ST funds. Gandhi contrasted BRS's 'Dorala' (landlord-centric) governance with Congress's proposed 'Prajala' (people-centric) government. The Telangana assembly elections are scheduled for November 30, with vote counting on December 3. Major parties include the ruling BRS, Congress, and BJP.

article_content: A newborn survived after being born on a train toilet and falling through the chute onto the tracks. The 22-year-old mother experienced sudden labor pains and delivered the baby in the restroom as the train approached Hanumangarh station in Rajasthan. Senior railway police official Subhash Vishnoi stated: 'The infant slipped through the toilet chute onto the tracks while the mother lost consciousness.' Most Indian trains feature squat toilets with direct track drainage systems. After the train departed, family members discovered the unconscious mother. Railway personnel located the crying newborn on the tracks and transported him to a hospital. Police official Ram Singh noted: 'The parents were relieved to find their child alive and unharmed.' The mother was later transferred to Hanumangarh Hospital, while the baby received initial treatment at a local facility before being moved to a larger hospital. Chief medical officer Dr. SP Rohilla confirmed both patients are stable, with the baby showing no major injuries despite being underweight at birth.

article_content: Approximately 3,600 retail employees face uncertain futures as outdoor specialist Blacks Leisure prepares for potential administration. The troubled retailer, operating 98 Blacks outlets and 208 Millets stores, reported £36m in debt with £16m losses during 2011's first half. Despite acquisition talks with outdoor apparel firms Edinburgh Woollen Mill and Mountain Warehouse, rescue prospects remain dim. Britain's high street crisis deepens with multiple retailers struggling. Carpetright reported £800,000 losses between May-October 2011, reversing previous £9.8m profits. Thomas Cook plans 200 store closures affecting 1,000 jobs through its Co-Op travel merger. Unseasonably warm autumn weather compounded problems for outdoor retailers, with Arcadia and John Lewis confirming seasonal sales declines. Recent months saw Comet sold for £2 after £22m losses, La Senza restructuring 158 stores (2,600 jobs at risk), and Cadbury cutting 200 positions at its Bournville plant. Blacks Leisure now considers a pre-pack administration deal - a rapid asset sale process - after failed acquisition attempts including collapsed talks with Mike Ashley's Sports Direct. Industry analysts highlight this as part of broader retail challenges affecting UK employment.

article_content: A two-year-old Arizona boy died after being caught in a pit bull attack while under a babysitter's care. Daniel was staying with a 28-year-old babysitter in Gilbert when three dogs began fighting around 11am Sunday. The caregiver sustained injuries while trying to separate the animals from the child. Emergency responders transported Daniel to Gilbert Mercy Medical Center where he was pronounced dead. The babysitter underwent surgery at Scottsdale Healthcare Osborn Medical Center and remains in stable condition. Maricopa County Animal Control has quarantined the dogs for 10 days while authorities investigate. Daniel's mother, who was in Flagstaff during the incident, described being 'numb' upon learning of her son's death. Police currently classify the event as a tragic accident but note charges could be filed pending investigation results. Four other children present (two 9-year-old boys and two girls aged 6 and 7) escaped unharmed.

article_content: Authorities are conducting a nationwide search for a suspect involved in shooting two police officers during bank robbery incidents across Georgia and Mississippi. FBI Special Agent Daniel McMullen warned the public: 'Do not confront this individual - contact law enforcement immediately as he is armed and dangerous.' The suspect first attempted a bank robbery in Atlanta, Georgia on December 23 before successfully robbing another bank in Tupelo, Mississippi approximately 300 miles west. During the Mississippi confrontation, Officer Gale Stauffer was fatally shot and Officer Joseph Maher critically injured. Over 300 police vehicles participated in Friday's funeral procession for Stauffer, an eight-year veteran survived by his wife and two children (ages 2 and 6). Tupelo Police Chief Bart Aguirre noted this was the department's first line-of-duty death among its 109 officers and two dozen civilian staff. The injured Officer Maher, 27, has been moved from intensive care to a private room and is beginning physical rehabilitation. A combined $200,000 reward from the FBI and local businesses is offered for information leading to the suspect's capture. The suspect is described as 5'8"-6' tall with a slender build, last seen wearing a ski mask, patterned jacket, khaki pants, black gloves, and tennis shoes. Authorities believe he may be traveling in a gray late-model Chrysler 200 sedan.

article_content: A cikin 1988, Taiwan na shiryin ƙirƙirar bam din nukiliya kuma yana shirin gwaji, amma wani masanin kimiyya na soja Cheng ya hana shi. Cheng wanda yake mataimakin darakta a Cibiyar Binciken Makamashin Nukiliya ta Taiwan, ya tura iyalansa hutu a Japan a 1988 sannan ya ƙaura zuwa Amurka a 1990. Yanzu 'yan Taiwan suna kiransa 'maci amana', amma Cheng ya ce ya yi hijira don kare zaman lafiya a Tsaka. China mai adawa da Taiwan ta fara shirin nukiliya a cikin 1960s. Bayan bala'in nukiliya na Chernobyl a 1986 (wani babban hatsari a Ukraine), Cheng ya yanke shawarar cimma yarjejeniyar da Amurka don hana Taiwan samun bam. Ya yi hijira tare da taimakon CIA a 1990, ya kwashe bayanai masu mahimmanci kuma ya zauna a Idaho. An dakatar da shirin nukiliya bayan wata ɗaya kacal. Har yanzu akwai muhawara kan ko aikinsa na jaruntaka ne ko cin amana.
translated_content: In 1988, Taiwan was on the brink of nuclear weapons testing when scientist Cheng Hsien-yi derailed the program. As deputy director at Taiwan's Nuclear Energy Research Institute, Cheng orchestrated his family's 'vacation' to Japan before defecting to the US in 1990 with CIA assistance.
